newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat price continues downward trend.
newsitem.headline: German wheat price continues downward trend.

text.p: Supply pressure from a number of European origins and a change in sellers' attitude reduced German wheat prices in thin trade, brokers said on Wednesday.
"More wheat is coming forward from farmers and co-operatives, but sellers are in no hurry," one said.
"Eastern European business is also on hold for now because of liquidity problems," he added.

Bread wheat consumers in Europe were buying in France and northern European feed grain buyers had ample choice of Danish and British supplies for spot dates as well as into the first half of 1997, brokers said.
A bearish trend in Chicago, where lower wheat prices reflected competition by major suppliers to the world market, also weighed on sentiment.
While EU cereals managers had raised their rebates to a generous 13 Ecus per tonne from 6.90 Ecus previously, they seemed determined to keep wheat volumes low, brokers said.
"Weekly exports out of Brussels might get stuck in a 200,000 to 300,000 tonne range in the next few weeks and the share of German wheat could be quite low," one said.
Free Hamburg premium wheat last traded at 287.50 marks a tonne.
British feed wheat was at 265 marks cif North Germany nearby and 1997 dates were available at 270-280.
The Hamburg grain exchange this week dropped its bread wheat price (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) and its spot feed wheat price free Hamburg by 2.50 marks each to 282.50 and 272.50 respectively.

In the fob Baltic export market, 12 percent material was quoted a few marks lower in a 285-290 mark range, 13 percent wheat was also a touch lower at 291-300 marks andwith 14 percent cost a steady 3110-315.
Barley prices headed lower amid EU supply pressure, lacking third country demand and thin domestic trades.
Fob barley was quoted in a 255-270 marks range, with domestic trades free Hamburg reported unchanged at 257.50.
Rye demand was also subdued with the exception of some southern German demand for milling qualities. Fob rye was in a 255-267.50 marks range.
The intervention buying season starts on Friday, November 1, but traders expected few initial sales at the 230.50 mark minimum price. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
